vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m1-t2.title: Sparse Matrix Processing (3-tuple Representation, Addition & Transpose)
vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m1-t2.simpleConcept: Think of a spreadsheet where 95% of cells are blank: storing every empty cell wastes memory and printing paper. In Lab 2, we store only the non-empty cells as a 3-tuple table (row, column, value), and implement addition and matrix transpose directly on this compressed list.
vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m1-t2.technicalConcept:
Program 2 performs sparse matrix operations using 3-tuple representation.
• Representation: Array of structs `Term { int row, col, val; }` where row 0 holds metadata `(M, N, K)`.
• Sparse Addition: Merges two sparse matrices `A` and `B` into `C`:
  - Compare positions: if `A.row == B.row` and `A.col == B.col`, sum values: `C.val = A.val + B.val`.
  - Otherwise, insert the term with the smaller coordinate first (row-major order).
• Fast Transpose: Swaps `(row, col)` coordinates and uses `row_terms[]` and `starting_pos[]` to achieve $O(Cols + Terms)$ linear time.
keyPoints: Triplet structure stores row, column, and non-zero value.
Row 0 stores header metadata: matrix rows, columns, and total non-zero elements.
Sparse addition merges two sorted coordinate lists in O(termsA + termsB) time.
Fast transpose achieves linear O(columns + terms) runtime using prefix starting positions.

examModelAnswers.question: Write a C program to implement 3-tuple sparse matrix representation and perform matrix addition.
examModelAnswers.stepByStepAnswer:
1. Data Structure:
```c
typedef struct { int row, col, val; } Term;
Term a[100], b[100], c[100];
```
2. Header Initialization: `a[0].row = R; a[0].col = C; a[0].val = count;`
3. Addition Algorithm:
Compare coordinates `(a[i].row, a[i].col)` with `(b[j].row, b[j].col)`:
• Equal coordinates: `c[k].val = a[i].val + b[j].val; i++; j++; k++;`
• a comes first: copy `a[i]` to `c[k]`; advance `i` and `k`.
• b comes first: copy `b[j]` to `c[k]`; advance `j` and `k`.
4. Copy remaining elements from whichever matrix still has terms left.

vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m1-t4.title: Printer Queue Simulation (Enqueue/Dequeue/Job Count/Overflow/Underflow)
vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m1-t4.simpleConcept: Think of an office network printer: 10 people send documents to print. The printer cannot print them all simultaneously, so it lines them up in a FIFO Queue (First-In, First-Out). The first document sent is printed first. We track current job count, remaining capacity, and notify users if the print queue is completely full.
vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m1-t4.technicalConcept:
Program 4 simulates an Operating System print spooler using a FIFO Queue.
• Structure: `struct PrintJob { int jobId; char user[30]; int pages; };`
• Core Mechanism:
  - Enqueue (Submit Job): Inserts at `rear = (rear + 1) % MAX`.
  - Dequeue (Print Job): Removes from `front = (front + 1) % MAX`.
  - Job Count Telemetry: Calculates active jobs using `count = (rear - front + 1)` (or dedicated `jobCount` counter variable).
  - Overflow: Rejects new jobs when queue buffer is saturated.
keyPoints: Simulates OS print spooling using FIFO discipline.
Jobs maintain metadata: Job ID, username, page count.
Job counter increments on enqueue and decrements on dequeue.
Prevents false overflow via circular queue implementation.

examModelAnswers.question: Write a C program to simulate a printer queue using circular queue. Include Job ID, user name, and page count in each job.
examModelAnswers.stepByStepAnswer:
1. Job Structure:
```c
struct Job { int id; char user[20]; int pages; };
struct Job q[MAX];
int front = -1, rear = -1, count = 0;
```
2. Enqueue Job:
• Check `if (count == MAX)` -> 'Queue Overflow'.
• If empty (`front == -1`), `front = rear = 0`.
• Else `rear = (rear + 1) % MAX`.
• Copy job into `q[rear]`; increment `count++`.
3. Dequeue Job:
• Check `if (count == 0)` -> 'Queue Underflow'.
• Read `job = q[front]`.
• If `front == rear`, `front = rear = -1`.
• Else `front = (front + 1) % MAX`.
• Decrement `count--`; return `job`.
examModelAnswers.markingTip: Award 2 marks for struct, 4 marks for enqueue with wrap, 3 marks for dequeue, and 1 mark for job count telemetry.

vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m1-t5.title: Polynomial Addition using Singly Circular Linked List (SCLL with Header)
vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m1-t5.simpleConcept: Think of an Olympic running track that loops back to the start line (Header node): on the track are runners carrying polynomial terms (like 4x³ or 2x). Because the track is a circle, the last runner points right back to the referee at the start line (Header). This eliminates tricky NULL pointer edge cases when adding polynomials!
vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m1-t5.technicalConcept:
Program 5 implements polynomial addition using a Singly Circular Linked List with a dummy Header node.
• Node Structure: `struct PolyNode { int coeff, exp; struct PolyNode *next; };`
• Dummy Header Node: `head->exp = -1; head->next = head;` (Signifies list start and loop termination).
• Polynomial Addition Algorithm:
  - Pointers `p1` and `p2` start at `poly1->next` and `poly2->next`.
  - Loop until both return to their respective header nodes (`p1 != poly1 && p2 != poly2`).
  - If `p1->exp == p2->exp`: add coefficients; append if non-zero; advance both.
  - If `p1->exp > p2->exp`: append `p1` term; advance `p1`.
  - If `p2->exp > p1->exp`: append `p2` term; advance `p2`.
  - Attach remaining terms until reaching header node.
keyPoints: Dummy Header node stores sentinel exponent -1 and points to itself initially.
Circular structure eliminates special-case NULL pointer checks.
Loop terminates cleanly when pointer returns back to the header node.
Terms must be maintained in descending exponent order for linear O(n1 + n2) addition.

vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m1-t6.title: Binary Tree Construction & Traversals (Level-order, Pre/In/Postorder)
vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m1-t6.simpleConcept: Think of a corporate organization chart with the CEO at the root: Inorder visits departments from left to right; Preorder introduces the manager first before the team; Postorder visits team members before reporting to the manager; and Level-order surveys the company floor by floor from the top penthouse down using a Queue!
vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m1-t6.technicalConcept:
Program 6 implements Binary Tree construction and four classic traversals.
• Tree Construction: Recursive function creating nodes from input (or reading null markers `0` / `-1`).
• Traversals:
  - Preorder (D-L-R): Root -> Left -> Right
  - Inorder (L-D-R): Left -> Root -> Right
  - Postorder (L-R-D): Left -> Right -> Root
  - Level-Order (Breadth-First): Uses a FIFO Queue of `Node*` pointers. Enqueue root; while queue not empty: dequeue node, print data, enqueue left child, enqueue right child.
keyPoints: Recursive creation dynamically instantiates left and right subtrees.
Preorder, Inorder, and Postorder are Depth-First Traversals implemented via recursion.
Level-Order is Breadth-First Traversal implemented via an explicit Queue.
Level-order traversal visits nodes level by level from left to right.

examModelAnswers.question: Write a C program to create a binary tree and implement Level-order traversal along with Inorder, Preorder, and Postorder traversals.
examModelAnswers.stepByStepAnswer:

```c

```
2. Recursive Depth-First Traversals:
• Inorder: `inorder(root->left); printf("%d ", root->data); inorder(root->right);`
• Preorder: `printf("%d ", root->data); preorder(root->left); preorder(root->right);`
• Postorder: `postorder(root->left); postorder(root->right); printf("%d ", root->data);`

3. Level-Order Traversal (Breadth-First):
• Enqueue `root`.
• While queue has nodes:
  - Dequeue `curr` and print.
  - If `curr->left != NULL`, enqueue `curr->left`.
  - If `curr->right != NULL`, enqueue `curr->right`.

vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m2-t1.title: Infix to Postfix Conversion & Bracket Nesting Syntax Validation
vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m2-t1.simpleConcept: Think of a code editor like VS Code checking your math homework: before it calculates anything, it checks if every opening bracket `(`, `{`, `[` has a matching closing bracket `)`, `}`, `]`. Then it converts the clean expression into postfix notation so a compiler can execute it effortlessly.
vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m2-t1.technicalConcept:
Program 7 combines two essential compiler frontend tasks using Stacks in C:
1. Bracket Validation: Scans string. Opening brackets pushed to stack; on closing bracket, pops and verifies match (`()` or `{}` or `[]`). Stack must be empty at end of string.
2. Infix to Postfix Conversion: Shunting-yard algorithm using operator precedence and associativity.
keyPoints: Validates syntax balance: (), {}, and [].
Stack Underflow during bracket closing indicates unmatched closing bracket.
Non-empty stack at string end indicates unclosed opening bracket.

examModelAnswers.question: Write a C program to check bracket nesting syntax validation and convert valid infix expressions to postfix.
examModelAnswers.stepByStepAnswer:
1. Syntax Validation Algorithm:
• Scan string character by character.
• Push `(`, `{`, `[` onto bracket stack.
• When closing bracket encountered: check if stack is empty (invalid). Pop and check matching pair.
• At end of string: return true if `top == -1`, false otherwise.

2. Infix to Postfix Algorithm:
• Scan tokens: operands output immediately; `(` pushed to stack; `)` pops until `(`.
• Operators pop higher/equal precedence operators before pushing.
• Pop remaining operators at string end.

vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m2-t5.simpleConcept: Think of an employee database with 10,000 workers: scanning sequentially through all 10,000 names takes forever. Hashing takes an Employee ID (like 4521), computes an instant bucket index (4521 % TableSize), and lets HR find that employee's salary and details in a single instant step (O(1))!
vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m2-t5.technicalConcept:
Program 11 implements fast Employee Record Indexing using a Hash Table in C.
• Structure: `struct Employee { int empId; char name[40]; float salary; int isOccupied; };`
• Hash Function: Division method $h(\text{empId}) = \text{empId} \pmod M$.
• Collision Resolution: Linear Probing with circular modulo wrap-around `(index + i) % M`.
• Operations: Insert Employee, Search by EmpId ($O(1)$ average), and Display Table.
keyPoints: Uses division hash function: h(k) = k % TableSize.
Resolves collisions via Linear Probing: (h(k) + i) % TableSize.
Provides O(1) average-case employee record retrieval.

2. Initialization: Set `ht[i].isOccupied = 0` for all buckets.
3. Insert Function:
• Hash address `idx = empId % M`.
• Probe loop: `while (ht[(idx + i) % M].isOccupied && i < M) i++;`
• If `i == M`, table is full. Else store employee at `(idx + i) % M` and mark `isOccupied = 1`.
4. Search Function:
• Compute `idx = empId % M`.
• Probe until matching `empId` found or empty bucket encountered.
examModelAnswers.markingTip: Award 2 marks for struct and initialization, 4 marks for insert with linear probing, and 4 marks for search function.

vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m2-t6.title: City Road Connectivity Graph Representation & Reachability
vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m2-t6.simpleConcept: Think of Google Maps figuring out if you can drive from Bengaluru to Mysuru: cities are vertices and highways are edges. In Lab 12, we represent road networks as an Adjacency Matrix and use Breadth-First Search (BFS) or Depth-First Search (DFS) to determine if a destination city is reachable from your starting city!
vtu-ise-s3-1bcsl306-2025-m2-t6.technicalConcept:
Program 12 models a transportation network using Graphs in C.
• Representation: Adjacency Matrix `adj[V][V]` where `adj[i][j] = 1` indicates a direct road connecting City $i$ to City $j$.
• Reachability via DFS/BFS:
  - Starts at source vertex $u$.
  - Recursively explores neighbors (DFS) or radiates outward via queue (BFS), recording visited vertices in `visited[]` array.
  - After traversal: City $v$ is reachable from $u$ if and only if `visited[v] == 1`.
• Connected Component Analysis: Tests if the entire city network is fully connected.
keyPoints: Represents city transportation network as an Adjacency Matrix.
Uses BFS or DFS to determine path reachability from source to destination.
Maintains a visited[] boolean array to avoid getting trapped in highway loops.
If visited[dest] == 1, destination is proven reachable.
